neutral_facts.value: The accused, who were part of the same family, were involved in a political dispute with the victim, who was from the same village. On 15.11.2001, the victim was traveling in an auto-rickshaw when the accused stopped the vehicle and dragged the victim to the house of one of the accused. The accused then assaulted the victim with various weapons, including an axe, sword, stone, and knife, leading to the victim's death. The prosecution presented eyewitness accounts, a post-mortem report, and recovered weapons as evidence. The trial court and High Court convicted all four accused of murder under Section 302 IPC, but the Supreme Court modified the conviction of one accused to culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 304 Part II IPC due to insufficient evidence of a common intention to commit murder.

quotes.text: The Trial Court, by its elaborate judgment dated 24.02.2005, found all four accused guilty for the murder of the deceased and convicted them under Section 302 read with Section 34 of the IPC.

The High Court initially acquitted all the accused by its judgment dated 21.06.2007, but in appeal to this Court, their conviction and sentences were set-aside, and the criminal appeal was remanded back to the High Court for fresh consideration.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused 1 to 4, belonging to the same family, were involved in the murder of the deceased due to political animosity. They alleged that A-1 stopped the auto-rickshaw, dragged the deceased to A-4's house, and all four accused assaulted the deceased with various weapons, leading to his death.

quotes.text: The case of the prosecution is that the accused 1 to 4 belonging to the same family, and the deceased, come from the same village - Janda Venkatpur, Asifabad, Telangana. It is alleged that the sister of the deceased and the wife of A-4 were political aspirants and they contested the Gram Panchayat elections.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that A-3 did not share a common intention to commit murder. They contended that A-3 only used a stone to assault the deceased and did not participate in the initial dragging or weapon-based assault, and that the courts mechanically inferred his involvement under Section 34.

quotes.text: However, as regards, the culpability of A-3 for murder, testimonies of four eye-witnesses state that the A-3 had used a stone to hit the deceased’s head, he never took axe in his hands.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that for an offence under Section 302 IPC, there must be a common intention to cause death. If the accused did not share this intention, they may be convicted under Section 304 Part II IPC instead.

quotes.text: The law on Section 304 Part II has been succinctly laid down in Camilo Vaz v. State of Goa, (2000) 9 SCC 1, where it was held that: This section is in two parts. If analysed, the section provides for two kinds of punishment to two different situations.

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed based on the determination that A-3 did not share the common intention to commit murder, but his participation in the assault with a stone made him culpable under Section 304 Part II IPC, leading to a 10-year imprisonment.

quotes.text: Even though, A-3 might not have had the common intention to commit the murder, nevertheless, his participation in the assault and the wielding of the stone certainly makes him culpable for the offence that he has committed.
